Hitman Absolution is a great stealth game with great production values, the gameplay is a little bit different than previous Hitman titles which lead some fans to dislike this game, if you like Splinter Cell and Metal Gear Solid I think you will enjoy this one quite a bit, if you are looking for something like Blood Money then this is not the game for you. The game adds a new mechanic called Instinct which serves 2 purposes, to see the location of enemies, and to hide in plain sight to avoid getting your cover blown if you have a disguise (for a limited time depending on difficulty). The checkpoint system is completely broken, when you die, you respawn at the latest checkpoint but enemies that you have killed, subdued and hidden respawn, this is a non issue if you ignore the checkpoints or if you play in the higher difficulties, Expert and Purist. Graphics and sound are both pretty good, the game is pretty well optimized, I ran this back in 2012 with an AMD Quad core + GTX 560ti and it ran well on high settings. Overall I think this game is great if you keep an open mind, just treat it as a different take on the franchise and you'll be fine. Pros: - Amazing atmosphere - Good acting and script - Contracts mode adds replayability Cons: - Not much location variety - Checkpoint system is completely broken

The Gameplay is boring yeah. But really, I didn't expect it to be any different though. Do I recommend this game? Sure. Just for people who are depressed really. Other then having a slightly relatable character and realistic likeness of depression, it isn't anything special. Sure I would play it and other people should play it. It's just... well... Eh... Not great. Not awful. Sorta in the middle. I know this review seems like it's very negative; but it is very thought provoking and relatable to depressed people. TLDR; Has no luster other then realistic potrayal of depression and being thought provoking. Try it out if you want, it IS free.

First VR game I've picked up that really felt finished. Whereas everything else has felt like a demo. Pros: +Enemies and enviroments look great. +Having to manage the energy in your flashlight vs being able to see enemies coming from afar makes the game feel very tense and exciting. +The later levels are very difficult and require a lot of energy from you in order to survive. Be ready for a really intense workout to prevent being overhwelmed. You'll find yourself switching between slashing smaller enemies biting at your ankles to sniping spiders shooting projectiles from the ceiling. +Plenty of different guns and addons to unlock, giving you a lot of choices for how to play. +Very diverse enemies with varied attacks meaning you have have to prioritise what to kill and when. +Lots different stages. Each of which has hidden unlockables, and different paths for enemies to come from. They aren't identical either so you need to learn fast where to expect enemies to stay alive. Cons: -Not a big fan of the ammo system. Would be better to let you choose what to refresh. If you're out of ammo for a gun you want to use you basically have to choose a different one or go back to a previous stage to farm. I feel like this system could have been better executed to make it less tedious. All in all it's a very exciting, active, and fun game. I highly recommend it. It's also a great choice for showing new people what VR really has to offer.

I gave this game a proper ride of 54 hours (finished the game), unfortunately lady luck did not spread her legs for me (but her legs started to spread on Ch.4): You cannot capture a ship you just boarded. This greatly affected my experience of the game and my recommendation. For a pirate ship game I expected to capture ships or at the very least, take over a ship I boarded. This game makes you go to different islands to find a person that is willing to sell you a different ship class, and this is the only way to change you ship. The schooner ship I got by killing a captain in the beginning does not count to my personal achievements because that was not a 'Purchase.' Even the old game Seadogs let you get a few first officers to capture boarded ships, command a fleet, and you could also switch ships after boarding. I can say that this game is good if you ignore glitches/errors in quests and lighting/camera/frame rate issues. Things I like about this game: + The Cursing + The Sexy Women + Ship Battles + The right amount of weapons and upgrades + Dice Game & Raven pet (great ways to make money) Things I hated about this game: - Can't Capture Ships nor switch ships after boarding, and no Fleet - When boarding you do not fight on deck of the ship with your sword and guns like in most good pirate games - The steam interface seems to lock up the game for me. - Tutorial windows pop up and go away really quickly (they should pause time and let you read it) - Animals are a pain in the you know what and I find myself standing on them all the time. - You cannot just sail and look around your ship without being in a fight. - No spyglass Things need to be improved: / Sword fighting can be better, maybe make block last longer (you get better at sword fighting with practice) / The world traveling map where you need to press Y to pause time and select a nearby ship to attack or city to visit should be a little slower. Maybe adding the word 'New!' near the just opened island or area for a quest to make it easier. / They should have more mini games like poker and throwing knifes like in Quest for Glory 5 and make sure to have NPC voices in the background does not loop the same talk over and over again. / There should be fast travel in the city. / Having only one area that takes you back on the ship from an island is not good for some quests. Adding multiple areas around the island where you could go back on the ship quickly would make the game quicker and more fun. / When a bartender shows you a officer to hire it would be great to see your current officer side by side to compare. /The quest logs should have a city name of where the quest needs to be done (on each quest). / I do not like to see old quest characters that are highlighted on my map they should be removed after the quest is completed and the items like old maps in the inventory should also be automatically removed when a quest is finished. This game is better than the Org. Raven's Cry (but changing the game a little and making it like a new game was a wrong thing to do, just don't rush a game out next time) but still needs a lot of work to make it great. The game has errors like one time I could not go to any island (it would crash my game every time I tired) and had to restart an old saved game to fix the issue. Another error I had was when I docked in the city and my ship was sunk by the time I got back to it. Save on 6 or more different slots to be safe in this game. This game gets a 7/10 but if they fix the bugs and change a few things above, it will be an easy 10.

Great game when it runs. Continuing from the great story telling of the past games MP3 pics up at a time that appears to be several years after the events of the last game. You start out down in Brazil protecting a young wife and her older rich husband at a party. The story jumps around a little by including flashbacks and skipping forward a few days after some incounters. Max's look also changes from his self-admitted crappy suit back to his leather jacket from the earlier games to later his bald head and flowery shirt. The story telling has always been fantastic in this series and it is well done here as well. This time largely with voice overs from Max himself while you play, vs. the comicbook style images in the past. But it is as good as previous games and some notable names/characters pop up from past games. The game/gun-play are really solid here, since the game is in 3rd person and you see Max on screen it's great how they handled his weapons. You're always wearing a dual pistol holster on your chest and it's seen at times but they stick to that by keeping you limited to a max of 2 pistols which can include Mac-10s or other automatic pistols. You can also pick up 1 long barrel gun, be that a shotgun, AK-47, submachine gun, grenade launcher, sniper rifle, etc. If you are carrying that gun and want to use a pistol you then hold it in the other hand, if you want to dual-wield then you drop the long gun. It's a nice touch and better than seeing a gun on his back or disappearing/reappearing out of his back or thin air. Graphics are good, nothing amazing but certainly not lacking. The screen 'tears' at times in both cutscenes and gameplay, but that is the look they're going for so it's not an issue, but did bother me a few times. I get that b/c Max is a drunk and you're not looking through his eyes (FPS) then I think they use that for effect and realism. As mentioned I've had issues getting the game to run. I run Windows 8.1 and at first it ran fine, I had to stop AMD's Raptr game tracking tool to get the game to work, but once I figured that out it would run fine. Then it started crashing. At first it was randomly during cut scenes, then I reached the only QTE in the game and it would crash each time I failed (wasn't expecting the QTE and I use a Nostromo so I wasn't sure of the mapped buttons). Then it started to fail to load, crashing after the title screen. So I've been in touch with Rockstar's support and they've helped but as of this writing I've been able to play it once in the last week and am on the final chapter of the game. Hopefully it'll get resolved for me so I can at least finish the story and game that I've otherwise enjoyed so far.

Throwing yourself and shooting people in slow motion never gets old, though constantly watching cutscenes does. The game runs superbly though and looks great, with some of the better physics I've experienced. Be aware that the game is extremely directed, and you are constantly being pulled to advance the story (many times literally as the camera is moved in the correct direction). This is my biggest gripe with the game, and it makes it a prime example of games being overly inspired by films. You are rushed to move along in the levels, yet still they have added collectables to encourage exploration. All-in-all it is worth playing for the bullet time mechanics and physics if you can stand the story-telling, even though the story never really caught my interest. Also Max saltiness got really tiresome half-way through the campaign.

TO BE CLEAR, THIS IS A BAD GAME The idea is great, the game is horrible. Class balance is almost nonexistant, after trying them all the Viking has the most ridicilous active attack, beats every other class with just that. Doesn't deserve 84% recommended Steam ratings or 60+/100 ratings. List-a-complainin' like an internet feminist Game tries to be Binding of Isaac with skills and stats (skills and stats carry over runs) Game ends up being arena Binding of Isaac with useless stats, a lot of horrible items, and a (MOBILE) pay-to-win system with an OP minion. (the crystals are actually in-app purchasable, but since the Steam version costs money anyways you'll get a sizeable amount of them, but that is still not enough to buy all cosmetics and minions) No unlockable items, you can find anything anytime. Yes that's a negative thing. Still can't tell if luck or skill matters more. Stat system is almost useless , 2 points per level used on something like: +0.02% higher attack speed, +0.40 (not 0.40%) more damage, +0.20% damage resistance, +15 health. If you were to spend every stat point on Strength, at level 100 you would have +160 from it (I feel like I need to note the easiest enemies in the game have 185 health and deal somewhere around 50 damage) With some classes half, if not more, of the skills in the skill trees increase a luck effect (ex. Crit, Stun, Spawn tornado) on attack Often so much ♥♥♥♥ is going on you can't tell where your character is. If you don't get lucky with your items and potions, your chances of actually beating the 4 (+1 DLC )chapters are quite low, pure skill doesn't pull you through here. I only beat it once so far, and that's because of life leech and stunlock items. (before you just call me bad i've almost 100%'d Binding of Isaac, only missing a few challenges atm) Potions are good but strange, for example a lower speed potion has cancelled three higher speed potions. Feels like 90% of potions I find are positive, not like (pills) in Binding of Isaac. Item finding is extremely luck based, and a lot of them are useless. There's a ♥♥♥♥ing stick figure that earrapes you, runs in circles for a bit and explodes dealing less damage than your normal attacks and the explosion size is barely existant Traps that enemies drop on death do INSANE damage, some killing you instantly if you fail to dodge them. After 30 level ups my Viking could still not outdamage the minion, by a long shot. The minion levels up with you, but a level 1 minion still did more damage than a level 30 Viking. The first activatable Viking skill outdamages your DPS by literally 20 times, and has a regen of maybe 5 seconds. Recently they updated that enemies with 1000+ health show with 1K health and so on, not being able to tell the difference between 1900 and 1000 health. Health number space running out was only a problem with end-game bosses, so I hope they change the lowest limit from 1000 to 10000 instead. No Steam Cloud, but to be fair the Dev said it will be added. Postive stuff Some amount of replayability, but end of the day point is to beat the same areas with randomized dungeons and mobs on every class on 4 difficulties. Minibosses or stronger mobs spawn quite often and drop better loot which is fun. A TON of items, but is that really 'good' when many suck? Dungeons always choose one layout from a limited amount so traps don't change, only mobs & loot. Controls, graphics, minibosses and sounds are probably the only good parts of the game. (yes that's positive enough for the positive list, the game sucks so let me hand it a rope) This game is a hot mess, no clue of balance within bosses, items, classes or skills, events like a dungeon spawning are luck based as well, you're never promised a store no matter how much money you have since it also spawns randomly. This game is, to simply put it, horrible. And yet I love it, would recommend to anyone who enjoyed BoI.

This game is the love child of Binding of Isaac and Diablo. I've put in 20 hours sofar and am satisfied on one hand but frustrated. The game is solid but flawed; many of the things i have issue with are fixable and thankfully the devs are active in the discussions and have been posting updates and fixes regularly so these points may be non existant by the time you read them. 1 Multiplayer isn't ready though the devs have been keeping the community updated on their progress in getting it up. 2. Class balance needs work, there is one class far ahead of he others 3 Lack of immunity frames after getting hit leads to some near instant deaths at times. 4 stat weighting makes health the goto stat just to progress due to high high damage and slow movment speed and lack of defensive skills to compensate. 5 In level dungeons offer a risk vs reward mechanic that is often skewed towards risk due to bosses in confined space who's sole counterplay is mobility. leads to near instant deaths on a level 60 character in first zone. 6 Cloud support not ready yet so if you intend on playing on multiple computers you have to do some copy and pasting. Otherwise it is a charming game, the relics and skills look solid and with a little time this may turn out to be a fantastic game.

I got the game long time ago in the Humble Bundle and found it while sorting my Game Library. This game is now one of my favourite skill based platformers. The difficulty increases at a perfect pace in my opinion. It's also nice that you visit old areas/levels after getting new skills, so you can reach secrets. At some points it's really hard to advance and you need to combine all skills you have curretnly available. I advice you to use a gamepad for this game, with a keyboard it might be very tricky and cause frustration. At least there is a great soundtrack with lots of different songs and they are not annoying when you are trying this one hard jump for the 50th time. Some things that could imrpove the gaming experience would be more spoken dialogue, it's really alot ot read. Also some cut scenes and splash screens have a really annoying colour flashing, so I needed to close my eyes whenever they appeared before I got an epileptic seizure. :D As I said earlier, I'm now 5 hours into the game and it feels like I achieveved alot, I would guess I'm at around 80% completion and I can't wait for tomorrow to finish the rest and get all the remaining achievements aswell. The game even has a Cooperation Mode that I will probably never try, but maybe it's interesting for some people. The 'Super Turbo Championship Edition' (a polished version with some more content) is actually on sale now, so I would go ahead and buy it. Definitely worth the money if you enjoy platformers with a certain challenge.

Fun indie game. You and your team build a castle to defend either flags or halls(basically conquest mode) and then go and attack the enemy castle. You can build catapults, undermine the castle, scale the walls with a grappling hook, or blow the front gate open and storm in. Every match is unique and it's amazing to see what kind of castles and traps people build. There are three classes, builder archer and knight. The builder sucks at fighting and is pretty much only used to dig tunnels, build castles and ships, and in some cases run up and smack the enemy walls with his hammer. The archer has a bow(duh) and a grappling hook that he can use to climb walls/trees. The knight has a shield and a sword and has an interesting sword mechanic. This was my old review, I'm going to edit in my updated one that I wrote for the expansion. You might be asking yourself, 'What does this game do differently that makes it worth my while?' Well, in short, it’s not “yet another bad Masters of Orion clone”, It’s not “Civilization IN SPACE!” and it's not Sword of the Stars 2. What this game is, and I really stress this, is unique. While I have had a hard time getting into it (a fault of my own as you can’t simply zone out and play this like any other space 4x), it’s by far the most refreshing take on the genre yet. To go into great depth about why it's unique would make for a very long review but to have a few examples: * You can rebuild ancient wrecks and turn the war around, as if you were playing a space RPG from the perspective of the ragtag empire suddenly getting the heroic lead character’s assistance with the Ancient Relic Warship of Destruction. * And following on with that thought, said warship can then be used to blow up the supermassive black hole at the heart of a galaxy, obliterating the galactic core. Rival empire spiraling out of control? Not anymore. * You can spend political capital to rename your flagship. This inspires your people. Yes, renaming your flagship to “LongflongActual.” is inspiring. * You can convince the galactic council that a planet inside a rival empire should belong to you, and they will vote and agree on it, even as the rival in question desperately tries to stop it going through. * Someone put a bill into the galactic council encouraging research? The highest voter gets an extra bonus ontop of it. Watch as all the players race to be the most supportive of a bill that already helps them because only one can be at the top. All this, and more, because the core product has modding support and steam workshop integration. These are both great for the longevity of Star Ruler 2, and I'm certain this expansion will be the same. Now, you might be asking, what’s bad about Star Ruler 2? By being unique you will need to learn, and it can be a steep climb at that. You will need to be patient and want to explore something new but the wonderful dev’s behind this game have extensive tooltips and help to smooth that over. Can’t get the help you need or find it not enough? There is even an ingame IRC client you can connect to with no fuss from within game and ask. Get Star Ruler 2, and while it might date this review to say this, get it even with Stellaris on the horizon if you are comparing the two. This is A Good Game right now. A pleasant, solid reimagining of a genre filled with the wrecks and broken remains of so many alternatives. And it really never gets old to turn galactic politics into a wonderful game of “who’s bill do I ruin next?”

Star Ruler 2 as a game, has a rather steep learning curve, strange mechanics, good looking graphics for a 4X, and the ability for the players to design their own ships as they want to, in other words, if you are looking for a good 4X game that will remain playable for a rather long time and an affordable price, look no further, Blind Mind Studio pretty much nailed it. Yet there is something they did not achieve, it is failing to take the consumers for idiots, despite their best efforts: Star Ruler 2 is very moddable for anyone who can open a folder and use a text editor, but the game also includes a mod editor, directly accessible from the main menu, so anyone who finds the game lacking in some ways can adress the issue directly, and with minimal brain damage. Even if you want to do something a bit more advanced, the ingame mod editor allows you to create the basic framework, and do the rest by yourself using the third party tools of your choosing, all in Angelscript, a simple but powerfull language derivated from C. So yes, Blind Mind Studio actually failed to present you a dull, locked game that you would play for a few hours and then be bored with, they failed to wrongly believe the game they made would be enough to please you, they failed to understand what some big publishers figured out fifteen years ago: that the consumers are cattle ready to be milked, and that games should not be so easily modified. Here Blind Mind Studio made a game which could be better suited to one's exquisite tastes, so they made a game one can change. As such, Star Ruler 2 is more a game generator than it is a game, and its a great game.

A lot of 4x games nowadays (looking at you, GalCiv3) suffer from being a mile wide and an inch deep. Once you get past the front-loaded content, you have to work very hard to get something new out of it. Star Ruler 2 is the opposite. In the first hour or two of gameplay, things look very simple (and perhaps a little boring) from a card-based diplomacy system to a purely strategic style of combat. You colonize a few planets, upgrade them, maybe build a few orbitals and fleets to deal with the occasional remnants. Then you start finding your planets annexed by the ai because you were playing double speed waiting for something to happen, and didn't pay attention to the diplomatic events, followed by an immensely vicious political duel with hundreds of votes and half a dozen backroom deals as you try to annex the system to get your planets back. After you finally re-annex the place with a final vote of 394-yes/363-no, the big bad Oko aliens that have been conquering and vassalizing everyone else decide that they don't like you kicking THEIR pet vassal-dog out of YOUR backyard, so they stage a massive 2-prong invasion that takes you a solid 70 minutes to fight off as you rush every fleet you have to the front and frantically try to build more. Then, just as you get ready to counter-invade, they come back for another go: only this time you drive them off easily because 1) You discovered a new diplomacy card that renamed your front-line systems and gave all friendly units there a 20% combat bonus; and 2) You copied a medium size-32 railgun support ship design you found through google and it gutted the enemy fleets like a chainsaw through butter because they were primarily using fancy-pants liquid armor which has no DR. After you smash that attack with ease, you gear up and assault the nearest enemy systems (which is almost everyone at this point because of the aforementioned vassalization) and capture 5 whole systems before they can counter. So now you're embroiled in a multi-galaxy war where almost everyone is frantically militarizing for all they're worth and playing two separate 3-dimensional chess games; one where they try to hit systems without having to fight through the bulwark systems everyone has built, and another where they try to figure out the next perfect ship design to take advantage of each other's weaknesses. And all because you though diplomacy was boring, so you jumped to double game speed waiting for something to happen.

Only problem I can see is that I don't think there is Full Controller Support, I may be wrong, but RollerCoaster Tycoon World has it and I think its a feature that would be helpful for people who can only play on Steam Controllers.

You're used to this story by now, the industry has trained us to buy games that aren't complete. If the question is: Is this the RCT3 sequel I've been waiting for? The answer is: It totally will be in a year, and hopefully we won't have to pay more for it. In short, the core game is here, and fantastic. It is absolutely the true successor to the rollercoaster tycoon series. The bad news is it's got 20% of the content it should, and is the very clear product of a community of alpha testers who were primarily interested in their favorite pet coaster and elaborate, hyper-detailed scenery and building options. But the game doesn't even have as many rides in TOTAL as RCT3 shipped with in each CATEGORY of ride. There are a fair number of coasters but several of them are just duplicates of one another with minor variants, and there still aren't as many as shipped with previous tycoon games. The management is even more rudimentary than RCT3 and offers precisely zero innovations, the career campaign is as identically bland and forgettable as old games, and in many cases the interface is actually a step back, although they're tweaking it bit by bit. Oh, and that revolutionary 'guest brain' they spent so much time hyping in marketing? You'll just have to take their word for it that it's under there, somewhere. Because parks operate, and guests react, identically to the way they did in RCT3. There are absolutely no visible signs of this 'simulation evolved' nonsense they kept going on about. It's RCT3 with better graphics and less functionality right now, straight up. The game shouldn't have gone full release yet, it deserved and required another 6 months of development dedicated solely to expanding features and content. But the devs have promised heavy post-release support before pursuing paid DLCs, so we can hope that in a year's time they'll have actually completed the game and we can finally enjoy the next rollercoaster tycoon in all its glory. The degree to which you want to be upset about this shortcoming is up to you. I'm fine with it, but only on the promise that they'll actually complete the game now that they've sold it to me. But don't believe the fanboys raving about how it's already perfect. They're so dedicated to supporting the game that they're willing to lie to themselves and tell each other stories about 'omg how hard it is to make a game in 2016 compared to 20 years ago we should be so grateful we have what we do,' which is patent ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. The devs built a very solid core game then skipped the second half of development in favor of releasing it to the paying market, and it shows. But it's likely to only change for the better as time goes on. I fully expect to be updating this review to an unconditional 'recommend' within 12 months.

I never thought a bad game could be so baffling as to have emotionally exhausting gameplay and a painfully unplayable story, and not the other way around. With that said, this was, and will continue to be, my experience with Resident Evil 6. The story has been fragmented and plays out over four campaigns, meaning you never get the full story until you play through each one. While this seems like it could be interesting, setting the entire game up for a moment where everything suddenly makes sense, there are a lot of problems with the fragments themselves. They are cliche and are very boring to play through, and at some stages, I think the game does a better job setting up minor characters and their deaths much better than the hardly-ever-explained consistent protagonists. I'm sure Leon's story was supposed to be a slew of references to the zombie genre as a whole, but it's played too seriously to even consider; while Chris' story never explains where or why they're in a new location, just that they're there, and their squadron has more humanity in them than the cardboard cut outs the real protagonists have become. Then there's the gameplay. There are so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t mechanics I don't know where to start: You're immediately thrown into the tutorial without warning, and can't proceed to the main menu until you complete it; the game requires more button combinations to do anything, such as how hide behind cover requires you to aim down your sights and press space (even then your character might not actually look out from behind it); the game's clunky button prompts get you killed (I died because the game gave me a prompt to make progress through a gauntlet event, only for the prompt to jump down appear and have my character backtrack into certain death); you can't pause the actual game, only bring up a menu, and with little to no breathing time, padded out gameplay, and timed missions, you better hope you just passed a checkpoint that'll start you right there because you'll have to exit to the menu otherwise; the worst quick time events that make up for 40% of gameplay; the aiming system being unreliable, with your characters' crosshairs wavering all over the place; and every enemy and boss being a bullet-sponge, and in a survival horror game where ammo is supposed to be scarce, you're ♥♥♥♥ed if you run out. Too long, didn't read: Gameplay sucks, story is boring. Don't even.

Since the days of the PSX the Biohazard/RE series has been home to great SURVIVAL HORROR games, with likable characters and neat monster design. This game, while still maintaining its place in the RE universe in terms of characters and monster design, it is not a SURVIVAL HORROR game. This title is first and foremost an ACTION game and a pretty good one at that. If you enjoy Action/third person shooters then you will enjoy this game. Most of the negative reviews geared towards this game are from people who are upset that this was not the traditional RE experience. If this does not bother you, then you should ignore the negative reviews and consider this game as an above average action/3rd person shooter. PROs: RE universe and characters In depth combat mechanics NOT NESSECCARILY A CON: Action game instead of survival horror Keyboard controls are bad, recommend you use a DS4 or DS3

First, lets start with the Negatives: Voices: Everyone except the main chracter (who is a little annoying, but I personally like it) is bad. The doctor was passable, but thats it. The gameplay: Some of the parts are comepletly impossiable without hints. For example, why would I think to use the fire extisher to knock out a guard? Why would I ask the bad-tempered dude what his problem was 3 times?! Speed: Other than double clicking to instantly move, the main chracter seems to like walk very slowly , which can be annoying late in the game. Size: This game took me a half hour to finish. I Know this is your first chaper, and its free to boot, but couldn;t have added a little more content? And now for the good. Story: Intriguing. Why did this happen? Why has the city fallen apart? If this were a normal civil war, wouldn;t the city be in better shape? The amnesiac is typical fare, but the fate of the city is certinly a good start. Music: While loud at times, it was prett atmospheric and fit the story well. Its not particulry amazing, but it does its job, and well. Art: Cartoony, friendly, and well done. This Game's Design is defintly one of its strong suits. The end result: A far too short game with flaws, but in its defense, it the 1st part of a new project by indie developers. One does not have to work hard to give them some slack, and with said slack this was a fun and thougly enjoyable half hour. Yes, it was short, but I think this was a more of a testing of the waters to see if anyone was truly interested in this game, and it deserves some attention. And for pete's sake , its free! And when if they iron out the flaws I mentioned, it will definitly be worth spending money on (provided they don't ask too high a price, and that's a mistake anyone can make).

I'm afraid I can't be totally objective, but here I go. This is the demo of a game, which is great because it is free, like most demos. After playing this one -as a demo- I would totally buy the rest of the game... BUT only if Chapter 2 isn't as short as this one. What I liked about this game demo (besides the beautiful Buenos Aires): The Argentinian mood: we don't really get to see the city of Buenos Aires (other than a glimpse of the Obelisc at the end), but the tango-inspired music and the Argentinian accent in the Spanish version are perfect. I haven't played the other languages, but even the casual cockyness of the characters is very Buenos Aires. The illustrations are nice and simple. The voice acting was quite good (again, I can only vouch for the Spanish version), with the participation of a well known Argentinian actor. Only a line here and there sounded a bit forced, but in general it was great, sounded natural and authentic. EXCEPT for the laughter. The two characters who laughed were awful at it, at least in Spanish. The little bits of humor, including Argentina as World Champion for the 6th time, which made me laugh in pain. There isn't pixel-hunting for that one item that kind of mimics with its background and gets you stuck in the game for ages. There aren't ridiculous combinations of items. Things are pretty logical. What I didn't like about this game demo: The gameplay becomes somewhat annoying. To interact with anything/anyone, you have to double-click on it, rather than the usual single click, and then decide if you want to look, use/take or speak. The only reason the gameplay doesn't get to be too annoying is that it's over before you get annoyed. However, if I consider it a demo, that's fine. All the puzzles are 'inventory based' or just a series of actions, like asking more questions or using X on Y. These are all quite easy to figure out in this game. That's not so bad, but in the end it's not very challenging. All in all, I recommend anyone who likes classic point-and-click games to try this demo. I enjoyed it and now I'm curious about the rest.

Brutal Legend is an open world hack n' slash staring Jack Black as Eddie Riggs, set in a fantasy world of a heavy metal album cover come to life. I felt captivated by the story from start to finish, more than I enjoyed the game and its pretty rare for me to say such a thing. As a game, the combat was just there, other games do it better, but nothing does the unique atmosphere better than Brutal Legend. The story is simple, you're a downtrodden roadie working for an ungrateful emo band that costs you your life. From there, you're transported to a fantastic land made of metal and stone. Where mammoths have chrome tusks and spiders made of steel. Its a fresh take on any fantasy world. Nighttime turns into a gorgeous meteorological phenomenon, either with electric blue moons or asteroid showers. The land is getting oppressed by a demon lord and you need to band together, gather troops and lead an uprising to defeat him! The characters are straight out of the late 70s early 80s heavy metal scene. Everyone is wearing spikes and black. Men have big muscles, washboard abs, long flowing hair and the ladies are always petite with enough mascara to blot out the sun. All the characters have big eyes and I think that helps them convey emotion much better. Its a wonderfully acted game, from the voice acting to the animations. There's a lot of humor, charm and goofiness that I enjoyed. I'm not one that likes comedy in games, but it hit the mark for me. Its not all comedy, the game takes itself serious when it has to be. The cameos also helped. Seeing Lemmy from Motorhead as my healer throughout the game. Having Ozzy Osbourne upgrade my car's weapons was a lot of fun. Tim Curry as the supreme villain. With all the famous voices incredible performances, there were plenty of great lesser known talent doing a fantastic job voice acting. All the characters no matter how big or small all have personality and charm, even if none of them have last names. Halfway through the game, the emo starts to bleed into this world of metal and the new characters are all gothed up. Crazy haired 'kids' with striped shirts, Victorian dressed women in white dresses carrying umbrellas. While they feel more Tim Burton than heavy metal, they're still beautiful as villains. What 80s metal head doesn't want to axe crimson clad, metal teethed nurses? For a hack n' slash, its pretty simple, you've got an axe to melee, and another axe for magic. You can use the latter to perform guitar solos that you'll unlock different songs at shrines. These solos go in a mini game that's like a quick, horizontal Guitar Hero. Since you're leading an uprising, you'll be commanding troops and its easy enough. One button to have them follow you, another to stay, another to attack a highlighted object and one to attack what's in front of you. I think this adds a sort of uniqueness to the game. You'll rarely be fighting alone, you've always got a crew with you. One of the first things you do is liberate headbanger grunts with giant necks. Then get ranged laser weapons for the razer girls from 'General Lionwhyte's pleasure tower.' The names alone play up what the game is going for. That era when fantasies were cool, imaginative, 80s, death, skulls and weren't dominated by elves or magic. In this world, the guitar is magic. Your solos can melt faces, heal your companions and summon vehicles. There are double team maneuvers with allies that can keep things interesting. You're forced to ride giant speakers, getting carried by roadies to keep away flocks of seagulls. Ride on the back of a Lemmy's motorcycle to stun enemies. Headbang with your grunts. Another mission has you trying to circle a Kiss beast in a ring of fire. While I can't say it was fun, it still switched up the game play. Eddie can't jump or even run, you'll need to hop into your classic, customizable hotrod named Deuce. There are mandatory driving segments here and there throughout the game to keep the game play diverse, but when you're outside of a mission, you don't have to use it, but its far better than walking. I just wish the driving was better. The steering in particular. Its not a bad in earlier parts in the game or when you're in the big open world, but later on, some of the mandatory segments are just painful to play. You're in a car, essentially off roading with trees everywhere, the slightest turn can send you off course into a tree. Some of the segments are pretty narrow and start to drag the game down. Nothing drags the game down more than when Eddie Riggs sprouts wings and it becomes what most people call a real time strategy, but I call it a MOBA. Its a struggle, you as their champion sprout wings and command your army against an opponent commanding theirs. This is a lot different than just hacking n' slashing with troops at your side. You can fly and even still drop down to the ground to fight or perform guitar solos to buff your troops. You need to buy the troops with fans. Both champions have a stage or a gateway as their home base and you buy troops with fans. You get fans by performing a metal solo atop of a fan stream where a tower of a merchandise booth is then built over top of it. Its okay once you get the hang of it. I feel like this was a tacked on multiplayer facet of the game. I can't imagine some 80s metal head getting through these segments, but there's always an easy difficulty. The more booths you have, the more funds get generated to buy troops. In this particular arena, there are six fan streams. Two by each stage, and one in each of two equal paths. So the arena is in a circle and that's fine too. Now these troops have specific talents, like a rock, paper, scissors sort of thing. Roadies take out buildings like merchandise booths and stages. Bouncers take out mounted enemies like those on horses and steel horses. Its easy to understand with the descriptions. I'd say these MOBA / RTS are 5% of the game and they're just there for diversity. Plus you can't lead an uprising without having your army fight another can you? With that said, I grew to hate these painful battles. I'm no fan of MOBAs, but these just felt like a chore of a tug of war. I'd take a tower over there, but lose a tower. These battles took far too long. Death in the MOBAs merely respawns you. Outside of the battles, death sends you back to the previous checkpoint, which might have been a while ago. A lot of love went into making this game. Well love and money. It feels like no expense spared getting the big names, making an incredible, immersive world with fantastic art design. There are little details that really make it an unforgettable experience. Even Jack Black performing a live action introduction of him finding the menu in a record jacket. There are details in game like the wildlife. Porcupines, giant horned elk stampeding down a mountain and the ability to run them all down with your car. If not use your car's flame thrower to incinerate them. Hey this is an open world game that lets you be in control. You'll find plenty of side missions, but I didn't tackle any of them until after the main story was over and done with. While its not a home run for its game play or in game fun, but its so good because of its art style, story and portrayal of these characters that the incredible soundtrack is almost an afterthought for me. Its there on missions with you, and in a cassette deck of the Deuce, but I was paying attention to the character's delivery that I found myself tuning out the heavy metal. I never thought I'd pay attention to Jack Black.

to get a decent up or down recommendation of this, let me ask you how you interact with a different game: if you sit down and play ‘grand theft auto’ (or one of its many imitators), do you A: play all the missions, carefully aiming for a perfect execution of each one, or B: ramp a school bus into a helicopter and start victory firing a bazooka everywhere like a chimp full of bath salts? if you’re the former, got some sad news for you: you won’t like brutal legend all that much. a lot of core mechanics in combat are pretty sloppy, especially once you’ve got a lot of people involved in a fight. a lot of the driving segments are frustrating and the world spanning scavenger hunts are just a chore that’ll have you reaching for a walkthrough. if you’re in the latter group, then UP TOP DUDE! you’ll love it. to get a sense of the game in a nutshell, imagine you poured every doodle in your 10th grade binder into a 3-d rendering engine, then ozzy osbourne showed up to tell you how great it was and megadeth started playing. the world design is like the cover of a judas priest album and you can ramp a deuce coup off every part of it. at one point you kill a big metal spider, turn her corpse into a motorcycle, and race it to go hang out with lemmy kilmister (voiced by the man himself). i literally could not add anything better to that scene if I tried. in case it’s not obvious, i’m in that second group.

Picked this up for 99 cents, and I can't really say it was worth bothering with. The game is, in a word, unremarkable. The monsters are all boring and repetive, the color pallate mostly consists of brown and grey, the plot and voice acting are both bad, the physics serve almost purely to make navigating past boxes and chairs annoying, and worst of all, the gameplay was outright dull. You just sort of move around from point A to point B while fighting small handfuls of monsters, and hoping desperately for something interesting to happen. The game at least tries to break it up with the ocasional survival section, where you have to fight off waves of monsters, but those are honestly even more dull. There were some mech sections near the end, but the controls for it were just abysmal. The game tries to spice things up with an RPG-lite element, but it's nothing to write home about. You have three different characters, each with three different weapons, where each weapon has three different upgrades. Fairly standard stuff, nothing you haven't ever seen before. To the game's credit it at least has some replay value in the form of secrets hidden throughout the levels, as well as other things such as survival mode. However, the game was boring enough that I couldn't really bring myself to actually bother trying any of that stuff out. Overall, I'd say don't play this. Instead, do yourself a favor and pick up Trine and Trine 2, both much better games that were both made by Frozenbyte. If you're like me and were only considering this because you've already played them, then just go ahead and play them again.

Spending less than what a sandwich costs on the shadowgrounds + shadowgrounds survivor pack was money well spent (bought it on sale for 1,50€). Survivor is a good 'sequel' to the first, improving on many features. The new physics, the same (or better?) lighting, shadows and shaders for a game not really demanding, the hordes of aliens, with the occasional variety in them, improved weapons, skill upgrades, experience, fun survival mode, some secrets you can pick up to spice up the old campaign from now and again, a cheesy but okay story, fitting the style for people who like movies like Aliens but are fine with not taking everything so seriously. Not many bugs, I did have the physx problem, but a quick look into the community forums resolved that (had to download a legacy driver, then it worked just fine). It's refreshing to see when a developer takes an old idea, the top-down shooter with the sense of style of gunning down hordes of aliens, and mixes it up a bit with working ideas, adding what you can do in a fight; from throwing a grenade with the now-added grenade button, to doing a special attack, to fleeing, flashlight alters at least the spiders behaviour, to simple shooting, also having an alternative attack at your disposal, which varies with the weapon and also needing to be upgraded. The design of the levels and aliens are obviously inspired by many iconic films and characters, but still made in their own unique way which is appealing for a light game of this nature. There are drawbacks, some cinematic animations can be mediocre (animations in general are simple in nature), as with the voice-acting, but I can let that slide, seeing as the atmosphere and gameplay still holds up as giving much more than what I paid for.

This is just as good, if not better than the original Shadowgrounds. The voice acting in Survivor is better, the story is less silly, and the way the story unfolds by switching between characters gives the gameplay some variety.

Rating 4.5 out of 5 If you are looking for a polished, free to play MMO with great visuals and sound loook no further. There is absolutley no reason not to install this game. I'll admit the art style didn't jump out at me as attractive when it first came out, but after sinking hours into it, I can really see the wonderful style for what it is. Ok now for the PROS: -Character creation - offer enough variety to make a truly customizable character that looks cool -Tutorials - Great option to do the tutuorial mode at the beginning, makes getting into the game alot easier. -Character Development - The way that skill are leveled up and character progresses is very unique and exciting. -Sound - The sounds are impressive (im big on sound in games) The soundtrack is truly fantastic -Graphics - I am running a nVidia 760gtx and can run the game on or near full and maintain my 60fps. Loading times are nice and short , game overall runs very smooth -Combat System - This is really where the game shines. Sucha unique way to make it an Action RPG and not a buttton masher. You have to be present during battles against AI. The skills must be aimed and enemy skilles are telegraphed allowing you to either dodge roll our interupt in avariety of ways. Overall the combat is the best in any MMO i've ever played. And I've played almost every MMO starting with Ultima Online. -Questing - The quests are fun and engaging, there are a variety of ways to level up. The Cons: -U.I. - the ui is a bit clunky at first but once you get used to it, its fine. It is customizable so take some time and do so. -Art style - some people will not like the cartoony art style that is present. I think you need to play for a few hours before you make your decision. It makes immersion a bit more of a challange. You have to play for several levels before you become immersed. I would give it until level 10 before making the decision. In closing I haven't been able to test out PVP system yet so there is no review for that portion. And also end game. I just haven't played long enough to know. Overall I think if you are looking for an MMO you should give WildStar a try, it is truly fee to play and you risk nothing.

Smooth and sweet! I have to admit. I was EXCEPTIONALLY skeptical of this game and tried the free trial thinking I would hate it, and end up uninstalling it. I had just uninstalled Neverwinter, a title run by the same company that made another mmorpg. They used allot of elements in their first mmorpg (Star Trek) in Neverwinter and it felt so bad and horribly cloned I could not stand it. In TRION's Defiance, I was very worried I would be playing RIFT like character models. However, it was NOT the case. I was very surprised at how smooth the character was moving around and how engaging the story was. There are cutscenes and an over all story arc that pulls you into the world and makes it feel living. There is an opening cutscene very egaging and interesting to watch. It ties in fluidly to introduce your character and put you right into the mmorpg open world. This is a hard concept most developers CANNOT pull off. If you read my Neverwinter review, you would see how I was so dissapointed that the game has a great system of cinematics mixed with in game gameplay for the first 5 levels, then abruptly cuts off and leaves you with rinse and repeat quest hubs and over all compelling story. In fact, most games are like this. Or you do a bunch of meangless tasks to hit that one point in the game that unlocks a small video file to show you what is going. But it feels awaward at best and interuptive and more of a 'reward' for reaching this point in the game. In defiance, this is not the case. The movie starts and then the action and what happens next and how the movie cuts in the game is SUPER fluid with everything you interact with. I was so impressed with how this made up the world that as an FPS and as an MMORPG this out performed almost all games I have been testing over the years. Especially the F2P... I am just blown away at the quality and detail used to create the 'I am here, and have a mission, and it is important' feel of the game. The publisher uses NPCs that mix right in with the cinematic scenes. It is very generous to give the story telling in a smooth, interesting, and over all pleasing game play experience. When not doing the main story arc missions, you will run across 'side quests' or live events happening all over the living world. You have open world littered with buildings and forest and encampments well entrenched. There is no stretch of land not used to it's potential to create the living world. As you travel you can pick up these side quests and help some fellow troops pinned down in a persistant battle. You can help link up to a computer system or enter a gun fight to give aid to your fellow man in arms. These are the 'visible' side quests on the map. There are allot of activities and war far events that are popping up off the radar that make you stop pathing to your quest and end up fully engaged in an entire other aspect of the game. I often found myself heading to my quest objective marked on the map, only to run across my people pinned down by gun fire asking for help. As soon as I enter the live zone the objectives are displayed...perhaps other players are already inside progressing and I am much needed back up as an extra gun...You see, that is GREAT co-op mmorpg features that bring people together! A live, persistent world always doing things that, if done together (or solo) will reward and not feel meaningless. As an MMORPG this game shines! It also has arc falls that bring people together for mini raid battles. EXACTLY like in RIFT. This is a meteor like thing that drops from the sky and you have to kill off the enemies waves, and then strategically shoot at weak points in the crystal. The more people doing it the better and it was not surprising to get into a group of 20 easy. There are several mission types and enough things to do to keep replay ability at a high. I did say 'a meteor like thing' because I have no idea what the TV show has explained about these. As a player who never watches the series I was a little lost in the dialog at times. They talk about how it is bad these aliens are doing things or this technology does this or that...I was totally lost. But it is clear that you are human. Earth was attacked. Technology was to blame. And it is now your mission to help the resistant movement or something rather. So the story is given out on a need to know easy to take in basis. And honestly, I like it! It is interesting, engaging, and works perfectly to get us moving along the path. No 'You are hero fighting for wealth and kingdom' bull crap. A real cinematic and game play experience to push this fantasy world forward. If I had on negative point, it is that in character creation, you have a choice of voice for your avatar, yet he rests silent in the cut scenes. It also is not DEEP as other mmorpgs as far as crafting and getting lost in menus and micro managing your stats all over the place. But it gives you just enough to be deep and thought out. The skill system for example. YOu pick what kind of soldier you want to be and form this out through skills. You start on a grid and start with a choice of 4 points to start branching out in. Stealth, speed, damage, defense skills etc... I chose a cloak that makes me hide from enemiesrefills my shield for about 5 seconds. After I chose this base skill, all the other skills around it unlocked and I Start building out. I can give bonus to critic damage by crouching. OR chose bonus dmg to enemies rushing you...So you start to see, if you are a fighter that likes to hang back and crouch behind a object, you can build this kind of character to suit your game play. If you like to snipe, you can get scopped bonuses. If you like to rush it you can get bonuses to that. The developers logically and awesomely built the skills and game around letting you fight how you want. I have tried so many FPS and you have to do one thing or the other, and in general all game play is the same. In this, you are complimented to play at your rhythm, style, and nature.

An Amnesia that suffers from its title. A Machine for Pigs is a terrifying, hair-raising, dark adventure game developed by The Chinese Room in collaboration with Frictional Games. The game eliminates elements that were present in its predecessor as a move to increase immersion, and it works to a certain extent. No longer is the player desperately searching every nook and cranny for light sources to decrease their character's sanity and even their own. Instead what they are presented with is a more linear but story-driven experience. A Machine for Pigs tells a story that players can't help but want to find out more but at the cost of having to delve deeper into the increasingly frightening areas of the game. What A Machine of Pigs suffers from is its Amnesia title. The first Amnesia title, The Dark Descent set a new standard for survival horror-games, and thus the Amnesia title carries a big expectation. Many hardcore Amnesia fans may find this installment disappointing, as without a doubt they will compare this with the first title. A Machine for Pigs wants to tell a story, The Dark Descent wants you to wet yourself. Without the Amnesia title, A Machine for Pigs would without a doubt be an excellent horror game. If you love mystery, adventure but also want some 'squeal like a girl' moments, A Machine for Pigs doesn't disappoint.

A Machine For Pigs is a worthy successor to A Dark Descent, giving an atmospheric fear and heart pounding chases through unfamiliar places, the game tells a good story through narrative between levels and various notes and events within the levels. While it is technically more of the same, the game felt fresh and polished compared to its predecessor. 9/10

Looking back, I can understand why this game got a lot of hate. Obviously, it had huge shoes to fill, seeing as how Amnesia: The Dark Descent is one of the most well known and critcally acclaimed pc-horror games of all time. But if you take a step back, take a chance to look at all the intricacies that are in the game and the world it takes place in, it really does shine. The Victorian-era theming, the imagery for machines and swine, even the voice acting; it all has an incredible effect on the player if you let the story tell itself. Not to mention that the game has plenty of twists throught it, so it'll keep you guessing till the very end. Some may argue that the enemy AI is weak, predictable or bad, but being a lover of these games, I can say that the game gives you plenty of warning and even tosses in a couple of enemies as 'teasers' (ones that are scripted and can't actually harm the player) to prepare you to deal with them. As a successor to the first game in the series, A Machine for Pigs may be stuck in the shadow of its predecessor, but as it's own game, it stands out in a dark, terrifying way. If you enjoy horror games, or if you have been reluctant to try this game because of the negative reviews, give it a chance by going into the game with a clean slate. I promise it'll be worth you while.

I never expected a game like this to be short considering The previous Amnesia, and the Longevity of the Penumbra series. Though this was developed by TheChineseRoom, who also made Dear Esther, which was also a very VERY short game (1 hour roughly). On the positive side, the game is very immersive and promoted horror quite well in it's own way separate from The Dark Descent's technique. The story really drags you in but at times it can be difficult to understand with overwhelming literary devices and figures of speech. The reason why I recommend this game is that I respect it in the Non-Amnesia point of view. The game for me just didn't feel like Amnesia. It was still a very good game though, although I wish it were longer.

I have to say that there are definitely some pro's to the game, the majority of which are in its overall style. However, the game turned out to be a pretty big letdown overall due to the gameplay, as many other people seem to also complain about - and further, the developer seems like they haven't been that helpful with some big issues. I'll lay it out simply. The artistic style was the entire reason I got hooked into playing the game, right when I saw it. And I happen to love Greek mythology as well - or pretty much anything set in or focused around the mythology. I was super excited to play the game, but right off the bat I had a very big problem. The game simply did not load up for me at all. It showed a black screen, then the application closed. Thankfully, some people in the forum had a fix for installing some framework MSI that came with the game, and it worked for me. However, a good amount of people seemed to claim that didn't work for them and that they were just unable to play the game entirely. I've not really seen the developer respond about this problem, which is extremely important considering it's playing the freaking game! That's a big strike right away. There's a thread about the above problem in the Bug Reports sub-forum right now still. However, I followed along as I was still hooked in, and the above fix worked for me in about 5 minutes. Right away in the game, I noticed how bad the controls were. The setting changes don't matter, and mouse/keyboard vs. controller also doesn't really matter. The game has a weird lag in a lot of the motions, and your character doesn't function properly. You move relatively slowly for a bit, until your character can suddenly start sprinting if you're still moving in the same direction - however, the moment you hit any sort of incline at all, even if it's like a 10 degree ramp, your character comes to a complete stop and then starts moving slowly up the incline again. This happens all over the place, so your motion is really bad much of the time. Bringing that into combat, you have tough enemies moving around you while you keep getting stuck or bouncing around in certain corners or places. Also, while it is realistic that a person can't be sprinting and then immediately turn 180 degrees and keep sprinting, they can definitely keep a lot faster speed than your character. The same thing happens as with the little inclines. If you turn around, your character becomes a snail again for a short bit. Such a thing is really bad in battles when the enemies get around you easily. And speaking of battles - some of the characteristics are fine, along with a general collection of weapons. But again, the gameplay is poor in the sense that very often when you swing melee weapons all over the place, you can be too close to the enemies and the weapons just pass through or over them, which does not make much sense in a 2D game. Even spears did this at times - if I am jutting a spear straight ahead, it shouldn't pass through an enemy. Thus, the stamina mechanic was made more of a pain when half the time you lose stamina without being able to hit anything. Another issue is the UI in certain places - particularly in item descriptions and in the shops. The descriptions for some items, if long, will run off the screen even if you are in the max resolution for your PC. But more importantly, once you unlock enough items, you will be unable to buy some of them in the shops. The shops keep the items in a vertical list, and you'll eventually hit a limit where items will run off of the screen and you can't select them. There's even a thread about this right now ('Cloak and Dagger...' in the General Discussions). In fact, there's a good amount of Bug Reports threads and the developer seems to not really be around much or care. There's more things I could go on about, including a good amount of lag in places too, but I don't want to sit here going on forever. The controls and gameplay overall are some of the biggest critical problems with Apotheon. I tried to give the game my best try and completed it simply because I wanted to witness all of the style, but it is really a pain in many places due to its problems. I can't willingly tell someone else to buy the game because I am sure there are many people who will hate it due to the above implementation issues.

Learning isn’t really a popular theme for video games these days it seems. I find that a real shame, as there is not much that can be more immersive than a well-made video game. Being dropped into the middle of a strange culture, and absorbing every aspect of it is supremely satisfying for both spirit and mind. As someone who knows quite a bit about Greek mythology, it’s quite obvious that the team over at Alientrap has done their homework as well. The weapons are all standard fare for the time, and can each serve a different purpose. There are ranged and melee weapons, but in a pinch your can throw your melee weapon with the middle mouse button. Just try not to break them all before you find a replacement. The durability on weapons adds greatly to the survival aspect of this game, but is really only the tip of the iceberg. There is a lot here to be excited about, so let’s get into it and take a deeper look at Apotheon. The story revolves around a Greek warrior named Nikandreos, who has been sent by the goddess Hera to kill her god-husband Zeus as punishment for abandoning the people of Greece. Along the way you will fight Zeus’ brothers, daughters, and sons. As you defeat them, you will be powered up. Artemis’ Bow will allow you to fire arrows faster, Apollo’s Lyre will illuminate the dark so a torch isn’t a complete necessity. Before you fight the gods, you will need to complete objectives within their realm. These usually consist of “find this” but some are a bit more thought out. Stealthing around a Satyr party to smash all their wine and make them leave is bliss. Make good use of your Assassin’s Dagger, which does 600% damage from behind. It might also be a good idea to craft some stealth potions… Or you can craft a bunch of explosives and healing salves, and just go Rambo on them. The choice is yours, and adds quite a lot to the replayability. On top of using a different loadout of weapons, there is also an advanced difficulty mode. Enemies have more health, swing faster, and hit harder… I wouldn’t recommend it to start with due to the quick nature of the combat. The aesthetic in the game really captured me, it is all based on the Greek art commonly seen on all manner of decor of the time. When the game goes extremely dark, you might notice that the dark nothingness appears to be made of stone. Major kudos to the guy who thought that one up. I just wish the music was able to keep pace with the graphics, but unfortunately, to me it falls a bit short. It’s not that the music breaks the mood, or isn’t enjoyable. I just found that the songs didn’t really stick with me. Still, the multitude of creatures and heroes and gods that you meet along your path towards bloody revenge would be enough for me to want to complete the story, even if there were no music at all. There is very little criticism I was able to find in Apotheon. Some of the hitboxes are wonky, which can lead to a comical mid-combat moment of both characters flailing their weapons wildly and hitting nothing but air. The music is also a bit bland, as I stated previously. Overall though, I love everything Apotheon has to offer. The endless struggle to find a useable weapon and shield, the crafting of potions capable of amazing feats, and the terrific speed of the running and combat. The entire game feels very fluid, and comes together to form an experience that I’ve never had before and doubt I ever will again. While you won’t be able to write an essay on the rise and fall of Greece, Apotheon is a great game to brush up on your mythology. Or you can just enjoy it for the experience it is, which is great. But I think the tidbits posted add a great deal. Who doesn’t want to read a little passage about Apollo? And once you’re done learning about him, you can murder him! Huge thanks to the folks at Alientrap for developing something that is so much fun, and even slightly edifying. Summary: Greek action-adventure peppered with survival elements and lessons on mythology. Final Score: 8/10 for aesthetic, story, replayability, and education. Apotheon is fun. The artwork is beautiful, the gods and mythos interesting, the gameplay is fun, and there's both enough challenge and slack to appeal to higher and lower skill levels. The game is not long in terms of its main story (it took me 9 hours total), though it can be fun to explore a bit and try to get the acheivements, or just bash some enemies, so there's potential to pad the run time, or replay. The game does have its faults though. For me, the controls were spotty most of the time. Areas that required precise and agile platforming were absolutely horrible, and when combine with the pressure of combat made for an entirely unenjoyable experience. The controls also prevented me from enjoying all that Apotheon's combat had to offer, since I could never actually do anything more advanced than flail a spear at my enemies. Also, the game will hard crash at times. The crashes usually occur when loading in a new area or cutscene, and the auto-saver does a pretty good job of covering you so that it's a simple matter of rebooting and hitting continue, but it's not perfect, and you might have to completely redo a boss battle if it fails (I did). In summary, the controls are imprecise and problematic, there are issues with hard crashes, but Apotheon will deliver what it promises, namely unique and interesting mythological Greek gameplay.
